history.p: Ludvig Holberg (3 December 1684–28 January 1754), was a writer, essayist, philosopher, historian and playwright born in Bergen in Norway but spent most of his adult life in Denmark. He was influenced by humanism, the Enlightenment and the Baroque. Holberg is considered the founder of modern Danish literature. His two hundredh anniversary was celebrated in many ways, and also Niels W. Gade and Edvard Grieg wrote music in his honour.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in cardboard with marbled sides and black cloth on the spine. Handwritten label pasted on the front cover inscribed: "Kantate / ved / Holbergfesten paa Universitetet / 3die December 1884 / af / I.P.E. Hartmann / og / Otto Malling". The score is divided into four parts: Nos. 1-3 in foreign hand, paginated 1-25; Nos. 4-5 autograph, paginated 1-42 by Hartmann; No. 6 in foreign hand, unpaginated and the last fourteen pages contain Otto Malling's autograph score to the second part of the cantata. Nos. 1-3 written in brown ink; p. 4 has been cancelled in blue crayon and replaced by pp. 1-2; on p. 17 four bars have been cancelled in blue crayon; in Nos. 4-5, pp. 1-23 are written in purple ink, pp. 24-31 in black ink and pp. 32-42 in purple ink; No. 6 written in brown ink.
